definition: A variant of gradient descent that updates parameters using a randomly sampled subset (mini-batch) of the training data instead of the full dataset.
details: SGD trades off exact gradient computation for speed and the ability to train on datasets too large to fit in memory at once, at the cost of noisier updates.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Boil it down and it is this: A variant of gradient descent that updates parameters using a randomly sampled subset (mini-batch) of the training data instead of the full dataset. Here is why it matters: SGD trades off exact gradient computation for speed and the ability to train on datasets too large to fit in memory at once, at the cost of noisier updates. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Stochastic Gradient Descent.
